entry_state: The report example preserves period, edition and both information cutoffs. Apple's asset notes constrain histories without identifying purchases or settlements. One cash-equals-additions history fails the nonnegative retired-value condition; two constructed unpaid-addition histories satisfy the limited asset book but require different company remainders. The proposed coupled offset is now being tested against individual cash-flow rows through an explicit allocation parameter alpha.
exit_state: A conditional offset preserves the annual rows only under the stated economic, tax and reporting assignments; no full Apple history is established. Different underlying liabilities still give different category and dated settlement paths. The next section separates lease use, liability and tax state, with the base two-payment schedule and a same-asset modification introduced; tax consequences continue next.
findings: Only alpha=1 preserves both cash-flow rows within the offset construction, and the text explicitly retains feasible-base-history and note compatibility assumptions.
The two settlement pairs each total -3082, while mixing their category endpoints invents a path. Timing changes first-date cash even when final cash agrees.
Quarterly disclosures constrain necessary remainders without constructing them or supplying settlement terms. No new confirmed defect.
